content.text: I'm thinking through how to approach this.

Considering an educational framing based on the omission of a constant offset in a linear prediction, selecting candidate papers to explain resulting residuals and correction limits. Initial focus on papers addressing influential observations, residuals, and diagnostics in linear regression. Chatterjee & Hadi (1986) provides a foundational overview.

Examined papers demonstrating the importance of residual analysis for detecting unmodeled offsets, particularly Combe (1973). Hastie & Tibshirani (1986) provides insights on additive modeling and backfitting, which iteratively adjusts for residuals. Friedman (2001) details gradient boosting, a method for sequential residual correction. Arlot & Celisse (2010) offers a survey of cross-validation techniques for evaluating prediction protocols. Efron (1986, 2004) addresses issues with apparent error rates and prediction optimization.

Examining Efron (2004) to address covariance penalties and cross-validation, revealing why additive correction leads to overoptimistic in-sample evaluation. Further investigation includes Buja et al. (2009) to understand visual inference and graphical hypothesis testing for distinguishing model misspecification from random noise.

Additive correction procedures iteratively eliminate residual errors to improve base predictor performance, as demonstrated across multiple papers. Stone (1974) details cross-validation protocols, crucial for separating prediction assessment from model calibration, avoiding optimistic bias. Gelman et al. (2014) focuses on predictive accuracy, emphasizing the distinction between in-sample error and out-of-sample generalization.
